issues.failure_explanation:
The theorem assumes \(v\in H^s(K)\), but the right-hand side contains \(|
abla v|_{s,K}\), which is the \(H^s\)-seminorm of \(
abla v\). This quantity is finite only if \(
abla v\in H^s(K)\), i.e. \(v\in H^{s+1}(K)\). For a general \(v\in H^s(K)\setminus H^{s+1}(K)\), the bound is not meaningful. The proof applies \cref{thmve} to \(
abla v\), which also requires \(
abla v\in H^s(K)\); hence the proof needs \(v\in H^{s+1}(K)\), a hypothesis not present in the statement.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either assume \(v\in H^{s+1}(K)\) and keep the bound \(h_K^s|\nabla v|_{s,K}\), or keep \(v\in H^s(K)\) and replace the bound by the standard estimate \(h_K^{s-1}|v|_{s,K}\). The source notation suggests the former correction.
issues.overall_effect: The node serendipity interpolation estimate is not established for the stated regularity class. The advertised optimal approximation property for the node space is unproven as written; either the regularity assumption must be strengthened or the convergence rate must be lowered by one order.
issues.title: Node interpolation theorem assumes insufficient regularity for the stated bound
issues.why_classification: The defect is a local mismatch between the stated regularity and the right-hand side. Correcting the hypothesis to \(H^{s+1}\) preserves the stated rate and the intended optimal approximation property for the natural regularity class; no new proof architecture is needed.
